title: Step 3 - a queue in a ring buffer
intro: `Queue[T any]` is first in, first out. Dequeuing with
`s = s[1:]` is short, but the slice's start only moves
forward: the array behind it never reuses the room at
the front, so `append` keeps copying to new arrays.
A ring buffer reuses that room. `head` is the index of
the oldest value and `count` how many there are. The
slots run on past the end and wrap to index 0, which is
what `% len(q.items)` does: the next free slot is
one, modulo the length. Like `Pop`, it zeroes the slot
When the ring is full, `grow` makes a slice twice as
long and copies the values into it oldest first, from
index 0. The ring is unrolled: values that had wrapped
